title: Open–closed weight devissage
statement:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be open with closed complement
$i:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$. If the two outer terms
$j_!j^*K$ and $i_*i^*K$ of the localization triangle
$j_!j^*K\to K\to i_*i^*K\to$ belong to $D_{\le w}(X_0)$, then so
does $K$.

proof.text: Use the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-weil-complex-weights]: $X_0$ is separated of finite type over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k$ is its fixed algebraic closure, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ and $w\in\mathbf R$ are fixed, and $K$ is a bounded constructible $\Qlb$-Weil complex on $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Base change the complementary immersions $j,i$ to $k$ and retain their names. Apply [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] with $\Lambda=\Qlb$. It supplies the distinguished triangle $A\to K\to B\to A[1]$, where $A=j_!j^*K$ and $B=i_*i^*K$. Its final clause says all three arrows are Weil-equivariant, since both immersions descend to $k_0$. Thus $A$, $K$, $B$ are $\Qlb$-Weil complexes in the sense of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], built on $D^b_c(X,\Qlb)=\mathcal C_X$, the same category on which [def-weil-complex-weights] defines $D_{\le w}(X_0)$; the three arrows are morphisms of Weil complexes, and the underlying triangle is distinguished in $D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$. Since the category of Weil complexes carries no triangulated structure of its own, this is what a distinguished triangle in the constructible $\Qlb$-Weil categories means. Its two outer objects are exactly those of the hypothesis.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: existence of the localization triangle for Qbar_l-Weil complexes.

proof.text: The hypotheses give $A\in D_{\le w}(X_0)$ and $B\in D_{\le w}(X_0)$ for the same real number $w$. Apply [lem-zl-complex-extension] to the triangle of step 1, with $K^{\prime}=A$ and $K^{\prime\prime}=B$. Its hypotheses ask that $K^{\prime}$ and $K^{\prime\prime}$ lie in $D_{\le w}(X_0)$ in the sense of [def-weil-complex-weights], a predicate defined only on the Weil complexes over $D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ described in step 1, so the lemma is applied to triangles of exactly those objects and no other coefficient category enters. Its conclusion is $K\in D_{\le w}(X_0)$, as required. No bound on the unpushed restriction $i^*K$ is needed: the assumed bound is already on $B=i_*i^*K$.
